author: Shelly Stallsmith
title: Biglerville senior learned a lot during Pa. Apple Queen reign - NewsBreak
text:
By Shelly Stallsmith ,
1 days ago Eva Hollabaugh was prepared to answer a lot of questions about apples.
It shouldn’t have been too difficult because the Biglerville senior has agriculture running through her veins. Learning about the popular fruit was one of the main requirements she had for becoming Pennsylvania Apple Queen in October 2024.
Her reign ended as she swapped her final soccer season for her last basketball season. She was the only returning starter from the team that made the PIAA tournament a year ago.
And now she’s preparing to close that season with the Canners on the other side of the District 3 Class 3A bubble.
Hollabaugh said her friends and family were very supportive of her decision to try for the crown.
“I thought it would be a super cool experience and it gave me an extra thing to put on college applications,” she said. “We have to have a bunch of knowledge about apples, but the main thing is just knowing a lot about the business in general.”
If that was the main qualification, she has that knowledge in spades as part of the Hollabaugh Bros., Inc. family.

Hollabaugh, who averages nearly 11 points for the basketball team, spent her reign making appearances and teaching people about apples. She spent a lot of time with kids and had no trouble with their questions.
Except for the one boy who asked “if an apple was falling from outer space, and caught fire, how fast would it land on the Earth?” Hollabaugh said with a laugh. “I was like, ‘whoa, are you kidding me? I can’t answer that for you.’”
Hollabaugh isn’t exactly sure where she’ll be going to college, or what she’ll study, but she’s been accepted into Penn State’s agriculture department.
And with all of her studying, she does know what she likes.
Pink Lady, honeycrisp and Ludacrisp are among her favorite apples, although her go-to this year was gold rush or crimson crisp. Her favorite apple dish? Dumplings, but apple cider donuts can give them a run for their money.
Pennsylvania has crowned an apple queen 76 times, but it’s the only time a Hollabaugh won the title.
“I was the 75th all-around apple queen, which is pretty cool,” she said. ''It was something I was really excited to do. We went to the Farm Show, a bunch of different schools, so I got to talk to a lot of little kids.”
She gets to take all of those experiences with her. And even though she might not hold the title anymore, the crown is hers to keep for life.
Shelly Stallsmith covers York-Adams high school sports for GameTimePA and the USAToday Network. Connect with her by email mstallsmith@ydr.com or on X, formerly Twitter, @ShelStallsmith.
